atoms.text: This guide configures the FlowTrace service to deliver load balancer access logs into an object storage bucket named lb-access-logs-prod. The bucket and the IAM role flowtrace-delivery-role both belong to account 111122223333. FlowTrace assumes the role each time it flushes a batch, which happens every five minutes. Create an identity-based policy that allows the PutObject action on arn:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/lb/* and the GetBucketLocation action on the bucket itself. Attach the policy to flowtrace-delivery-role. Do not edit the bucket policy, because a same-account identity-based allow is sufficient and no resource-based statement is needed. In the FlowTrace console, set the destination to lb-access-logs-prod with the prefix lb/ and select the role. FlowTrace writes gzip-compressed files named by load balancer ID and timestamp under the prefix. To verify, trigger a test delivery and confirm that an object appears under lb/ with the role as the writer.

This guide configures the FlowTrace service to deliver load balancer access logs into an object storage bucket named lb-access-logs-prod. The bucket belongs to account 444455556666, while the IAM role flowtrace-delivery-role belongs to account 111122223333. FlowTrace assumes the role each time it flushes a batch, which happens every five minutes. As the bucket owner, add a bucket policy statement that allows the PutObject action on arn:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/lb/* and the GetBucketLocation action on the bucket itself. Set the principal to arn:iam::111122223333:role/flowtrace-delivery-role. The bucket policy carries the grant, so nothing needs to change on the bucket side beyond this one statement. In the FlowTrace console, set the destination to lb-access-logs-prod with the prefix lb/ and select the role. FlowTrace writes gzip-compressed files named by load balancer ID and timestamp under the prefix. To verify, trigger a test delivery and confirm that an object appears under lb/ with the role as the writer.

This guide lets the TrailKeeper audit service deliver management event records to a bucket named audit-trail-archive. The bucket and the IAM role trailkeeper-writer are in the same account, 111122223333. TrailKeeper writes one JSON file per five-minute window, using keys of the form events/YYYY/MM/DD/. Create an identity-based policy for trailkeeper-writer that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::audit-trail-archive/events/*. Add a ListBucket allow on the bucket resource so the service can confirm that the destination exists. Attach the policy to the role and leave the bucket policy untouched. In the TrailKeeper settings, enter the bucket name, the events/ prefix, and the role name. Each file is delivered with the bucket-default encryption setting applied. After saving, wait for the next window and confirm that a new JSON file has appeared under events/.

This guide lets the TrailKeeper audit service deliver management event records to a bucket named audit-trail-archive. The bucket is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role trailkeeper-writer is in account 111122223333. TrailKeeper writes one JSON file per five-minute window, using keys of the form events/YYYY/MM/DD/. In the bucket owner's account, add a bucket policy statement that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::audit-trail-archive/events/*. Add a ListBucket allow on the bucket resource so the service can confirm that the destination exists. Name arn:iam::111122223333:role/trailkeeper-writer as the principal in both statements. In the TrailKeeper settings, enter the bucket name, the events/ prefix, and the role name. Each file is delivered with the bucket-default encryption setting applied. After saving, wait for the next window and confirm that a new JSON file has appeared under events/.

This guide covers delivery of CDN request logs by the EdgeLog service into a bucket named cdn-request-logs. The bucket and the role edgelog-shipper are both in account 111122223333. EdgeLog writes hourly gzip files to the prefix edge/ and assumes the role for each upload. Create an identity-based policy that allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:storage:::cdn-request-logs/edge/*. Include ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket resource so that incomplete uploads can be tracked. Attach this policy to edgelog-shipper. The bucket policy stays as it is, since access is granted entirely by the role's own policy. Configure the EdgeLog distribution to use the bucket and prefix, and set the log format to the extended field list. Large hourly files are uploaded as multipart uploads in 16 MiB parts. Check the first delivery by listing edge/ and confirming that the object size is nonzero.

As the bucket owner, add a bucket policy statement allowing PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:storage:::cdn-request-logs/edge/*. Include ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket resource so that incomplete uploads can be tracked. Set the principal in the statement to arn:iam::111122223333:role/edgelog-shipper. Access is granted through this bucket policy, which is the only change required on the bucket. Configure the EdgeLog distribution to use the bucket and prefix, and set the log format to the extended field list. Large hourly files are uploaded as multipart uploads in 16 MiB parts. Check the first delivery by listing edge/ and confirming that the object size is nonzero.

This guide grants the NetFlowCap service permission to write virtual network flow records to a bucket named netflow-records. The bucket and the IAM role netflowcap-delivery are in account 111122223333. NetFlowCap aggregates records over ten-minute intervals and writes them as plain-text files under the prefix flows/. Define an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::netflow-records/flows/*. The policy should also allow GetBucketAcl on the bucket so the service can check that the destination is writable. Attach the policy to netflowcap-delivery and make no change to the bucket policy. When creating the flow log in the NetFlowCap console, choose the bucket, the prefix, and the role. Each file contains source and destination addresses, ports, protocol, byte counts, and an accept or reject action. Files are named with the interface ID and the interval start time. Confirm the setup by generating test traffic and checking for a new file under flows/ within fifteen minutes.

This guide allows the QueryLogShipper service to export database slow-query logs to a bucket named db-slowquery-logs. The bucket and the IAM role qls-export-role are in account 111122223333. QLS collects log segments from each database instance and uploads them as text files every thirty minutes. Create an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::db-slowquery-logs/instances/* and attach it to qls-export-role. Add GetBucketLocation on the bucket resource to the same policy. The bucket policy is left unchanged because the role's identity-based policy already authorizes every call QLS makes. In the QLS configuration, set the export target to the bucket and the prefix instances/. Keys follow the pattern instances/instance-id/date/segment.log. Only the slow-query log type is exported, and only queries above the configured duration threshold are included. Verify by running a deliberately slow query and checking that the next segment contains it.

QLS collects log segments from each database instance and uploads them as text files every thirty minutes. In the bucket owner's account, add a bucket policy statement that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::db-slowquery-logs/instances/* with the principal arn:iam::111122223333:role/qls-export-role. Add GetBucketLocation on the bucket resource to the same statement set. The grant is made entirely by this bucket policy, and the role's account does not modify the bucket. In the QLS configuration, set the export target to the bucket and the prefix instances/. Keys follow the pattern instances/instance-id/date/segment.log. Only the slow-query log type is exported, and only queries above the configured duration threshold are included. Verify by running a deliberately slow query and checking that the next segment contains it.

This guide gives the LogSift analytics role read access to log files already delivered to a bucket named platform-logs-archive. The bucket and the IAM role logsift-reader are in account 111122223333. LogSift runs a scheduled job each night that lists objects under the prefix delivered/ and reads each file written during the previous day. Create an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on arn:storage:::platform-logs-archive/delivered/*. Add a ListBucket allow on the bucket resource, restricted with a prefix condition to delivered/. Attach the policy to logsift-reader and leave the bucket policy as it is. Configure the LogSift job with the bucket name, the prefix, and the role. The job reads files sequentially and records the last processed key in its own state store. No objects are written, modified, or deleted in the bucket. To test, run the job manually and confirm that it reports the number of files read for the previous day.

This guide sets up the PodArchive service to deliver container platform logs into a bucket named container-logs-store. The bucket and the IAM role podarchive-uploader are in account 111122223333. PodArchive buffers logs from each cluster node and uploads a file whenever the buffer reaches 64 MiB or fifteen minutes elapse. Create an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::container-logs-store/clusters/* and attach it to podarchive-uploader. Include GetBucketLocation on the bucket resource in that policy. No bucket policy statement is added, since the role and the bucket share an account. Set the PodArchive output to the bucket and the prefix clusters/, and select the role. Object keys use the format clusters/cluster-name/node-id/timestamp.log.gz. Each upload carries the metadata tag log-source set to podarchive. Validate by scheduling a test pod that emits log lines and checking that a file arrives under clusters/ within the buffer interval.

This guide sets up the PodArchive service to deliver container platform logs into a bucket named container-logs-store. The bucket is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role podarchive-uploader is in account 111122223333. PodArchive buffers logs from each cluster node and uploads a file whenever the buffer reaches 64 MiB or fifteen minutes elapse. As the bucket owner, add a bucket policy statement that allows PutObject on arn:storage:::container-logs-store/clusters/* for the principal arn:iam::111122223333:role/podarchive-uploader. Include GetBucketLocation on the bucket resource in that policy. This bucket policy is the policy that carries the grant to the other account's role. Set the PodArchive output to the bucket and the prefix clusters/, and select the role. Object keys use the format clusters/cluster-name/node-id/timestamp.log.gz. Each upload carries the metadata tag log-source set to podarchive. Validate by scheduling a test pod that emits log lines and checking that a file arrives under clusters/ within the buffer interval.

This guide lets the SecEvent SIEM connector ingest delivered firewall logs from a bucket named firewall-logs-delivery. The bucket and the IAM role secevent-ingest are in account 111122223333. A separate firewall service writes logs to the bucket, and the connector polls every two minutes for new files under the prefix fw/. Create an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on arn:storage:::firewall-logs-delivery/fw/* and ListBucket on the bucket resource. Add a condition that limits listing to the fw/ prefix. Attach the policy to secevent-ingest and make no bucket policy changes. In the connector settings, enter the bucket, the prefix, and the role name. The connector tracks the most recent object key and requests only keys that sort after it. Retrieved files are parsed as newline-delimited JSON and forwarded to the connector's event index. Verify by generating a firewall deny event and confirming that it appears in the index within five minutes.
